findings.where: Running text at both widths: the hero lead paragraph, the Surf, Vibe and What to look for paragraphs, the hero's 'launching across Indonesia' line, and the coming-soon notice. It is worst at phone width, in the notice ('MantaHostels   is   launching   across') and the lead ('workers   and   long-stay   travellers:   a').
findings.fault: Body text is fully justified in a narrow column, so the spaces between words stretch unevenly from line to line and open visible gaps and rivers. At 390 px a line sometimes holds only four or five words, so a line can be more gap than text.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker reading the guide on a phone, often on the move. The uneven gaps break their reading rhythm and make the page look badly typeset. That works against the effortless, crafted feel the brand promises.

findings.where: Hero, the h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu', at both widths
findings.fault: The page heading is in title case. The brand voice is sentence case, and every other heading on the page follows it ('Good for', 'What to look for'). So the one loudest line is treated differently from its siblings.
findings.who_objects: The founder and anyone holding the brand sheet. Sentence case is a stated voice commitment, and the mismatch with the section headings below reads as a slip, not a choice.

findings.where: Hero, the eyebrow 'BALI' above the h1, at both widths
findings.fault: The eyebrow is set in uppercase. The rules keep uppercase for badges and filter labels, used sparingly. A place-name label is neither, so it brings in a capitals treatment the system doesn't use anywhere else on the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, as keeper of the casing rule. Uppercase is reserved so that it signals a badge or a filter. Using it on a plain label weakens that signal across the site.
